name: galaxy-explorer
description: 🌌 An interactive, procedurally-generated Milky Way galaxy in the browser — WebGL / three.js, no backend, no build step. MIT licensed.

paragraphs: An interactive, procedurally-generated Milky Way galaxy — with a full 3D Solar System, a roaming comet, and real radio-galaxy jets — that runs entirely in the browser with WebGL (three.js). No backend, no build step, no dependencies to install, no API keys — just open the page and explore.

The galaxy itself is generated in code at load time: almost no image assets — the spiral arms, nebula gas, star clusters, distant galaxies and supernovae are all math (the Magellanic Clouds and Centaurus A additionally sample their star positions and colours from three CC BY photo plates). The Solar System layers real NASA-based surface textures on top for the planets, moons and Sun.
Free for any use — personal, commercial, academic and teaching — under the MIT License.
features: Spiral disc — 85,000 dust points on four density-wave arms, with a warm
core fading to cool blue arms, bright star knots, HII regions and blue clusters.
Volumetric-looking nebula — a continuous fBm + Worley noise shader field
(domain-warped spiral, dust lanes, glowing cores) that wraps the arms in gas.
Galactic bulge — a smooth multi-scale glow core that slowly "breathes".
